title.en: A bad neighbour is a misfortune

text.en: The Greek poet Hesiod said a bad neighbour is as great a misfortune as a good one is a blessing. India has more neighbours than most nations, and it has worked hard to turn them into friends.

India has Pakistan and Afghanistan to the northwest, China, Nepal and Bhutan to the north, Bangladesh to the east and Myanmar to the far east.
Sri Lanka and the Maldives lie close across the Indian Ocean.
With Afghanistan, the Strategic Partnership Agreement helps rebuild infrastructure, and India helped build the Salma Dam in Herat and the Kandahar cricket stadium.
India was the first nation to recognise Bangladesh and shares its longest land border, 4096.7 kilometres.
The Farakka accord of 1977 shares Ganga waters, the two share 54 rivers, and the Teen Bigha Corridor was leased to Bangladesh in 2011.
A 130-kilometre friendship pipeline links Siliguri and Parbatipur, and the BBIN motor vehicle agreement gives India road transit.
Bhutan, a landlocked Himalayan kingdom, has had diplomatic ties since 1968, and India built the Chukha, Kurichchu and Tala hydroelectric projects.
India and China are comparable in size and population, and both share views at the WTO and on climate change.
The McMahon Line, fixed at a 1914 conference, is the boundary between India, China and east of Bhutan.
China granted India observer status at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, while SAARC granted observer status to China.
Nepal is a buffer between India and China, depends on India for transit, and shares borders with five Indian states.
India built the Mahendra Raj Marg, took up the 5600 MW Pancheshwar project, and put the Nepali language in the Eighth Schedule.
Myanmar is India's gateway to Southeast Asia, with the Kaladan multi-modal project linking Kolkata to Sittwe and a Guwahati to Mandalay road.
India and Sri Lanka, separated by the Palk Strait, are friendly except for the Tamil ethnic problem, and India and Pakistan have strained ties with terrorism a core concern, tackled through the Shimla Agreement and the Lahore Declaration.
